title: Opportunistic trace hook + ID-mapper for legacy proxy paths
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Several internal and customer-facing paths traverse a legacy HTTP proxy that strips or rewrites standard trace headers (traceparent/ot-tracer/x-amzn-trace-id). As a result cross-service traces are incomplete and downstream services create orphan spans. We need a lightweight instrumentation approach that opportunistically attaches spans when a valid upstream trace identifier is present and maps legacy proxy request IDs to canonical trace IDs to preserve correlation.

Goals:
- Add an SDK-level hook + HTTP middleware adapter that: 1) recognizes common legacy proxy headers, 2) maps proxy request id -> trace id deterministically, 3) rehydrates context for async frameworks with minimal overhead, and 4) only activates when upstream headers indicate sampling.
- Keep overhead per request under 100us median in hot paths.
- Provide clear opt-in flags and safe defaults (no PII extraction, no unconditional header forwarding).

Non-goals: full OTEL shim replacement, broad header normalization for every protocol, or changing upstream proxy behavior in this ticket.

Approach overview:
1) Implement a compact header parser in the SDK core (Node/Python/Go) that recognizes: legacy-proxy-id, x-amzn-trace-id, and traceparent. The parser returns a normalized trace id when present. 2) Provide an "opportunistic" trace hook that only starts a span when a normalized id exists AND sampling decision is true. 3) Add an ID-mapper utility that derives a stable trace id from a proxy id using HMAC(keyed-version) to avoid collisions and prevent disclosure of raw proxy ids. The HMAC key will be managed via KMS integration in a follow-up. For now use a per-service ephemeral key. 4) Offer middleware adapters for express/fastify (Node), werkzeug/ASGI (Python), and net/http middleware (Go) to inject the rehydrated context into request lifecycle. 5) Add tests, microbenchmarks, and a dashboard to measure instrumentation coverage, orphan span rate, and added latency.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end trace correlation for requests that cross legacy proxy is improved: orphan-span rate reduced by >= 80% in test harness.
- Median added CPU time per request from the hook is < 100us on the standard benchmark fixture.
- SDK exposes config flags: enable_opportunistic_hook (default: false), id_mapper_mode ("hmac"|"passthrough"), and sampling_policy ("respect-upstream"|"force-decision").
- Unit + integration tests that simulate header rewrite scenarios and verify correct mapping and no PII in logs.
- PRs merged for Node and Go SDKs and middleware adapters published behind feature flag.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (internal): land SDK hook + test harness, enable for internal services only with feature flag. Monitor orphan spans and perf.
- Phase 2 (selected customers): enable for 2-3 customers that reported proxy issues, collect feedback.
- Phase 3: iterate HMAC key rotation + KMS integration, then flip default flag if safe.
comments: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting with infra and SDK owners. Agreed on opportunistic activation to avoid overhead on new flows.
2026-02-25: Spike implemented in Node SDK (branch: feat/opportunistic-hook). Basic header parser recognizes legacy-proxy-id and traceparent. Measured ~65us median overhead on local fixture.

2026-03-02: Design decision: use HMAC-derived trace ids for proxy ids to avoid exposing raw proxy identifiers in traces. Security reviewed by Priya (notes in Google Drive: /rdw/instrumentation/hmac-id-mapper.md).
2026-03-04: Discovered that some proxies rewrite content-length header; middleware must be robust but not alter body. Added tests for passthrough path.

2026-03-08: Created benchmark harness and initial Grafana dashboard (dashboard id: observability-legacy-proxy-corr). Dashboard tracks orphan-span-rate, hook-activation-rate, median-latency-overhead, and sampling-activation-rate.

2026-03-10: PR opened for Go middleware (github.com/redwood-inference/instrumentation/pull/478). Node PR ready for review (github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/302). Seeking review from @Elena and @Tom for async context rehydration approach.
